extract:
Icon Of Coil emerged from Oslo, Norway, in the late 1990s and became one of the defining acts of the futurepop and electro-industrial wave that swept European dark clubs around the turn of the millennium. The project was the creation of Andy LaPlegua, a vocalist and producer who had come up through Norway's small but committed industrial and hardcore scene. LaPlegua was soon joined by Sebastian Komor and Christian Lund, and the trio became the core lineup. The band was most active from roughly 1997 to the mid-2000s, after which it went largely dormant while its members pursued other projects.

From the start, Icon Of Coil fused the pulsing sequencer drive of classic EBM with the melodic, trance-inflected synth leads and anthemic choruses associated with futurepop contemporaries such as VNV Nation and Covenant. LaPlegua's vocals, often processed but always hook-oriented, sat atop dancefloor-minded arrangements that drew from both the harder Belgian and German body-music traditions and the brighter synthpop of the 1980s. The early Seren material laid out this template before the band's full-length debut.

That debut, Serenity Is The Devil (2000), established the band in clubs across Europe and North America, where it was issued by Metropolis Records. Tracks such as "Shelter" and "Repetition" became staples of goth and industrial DJ sets, and "Shelter" would later be revisited as a standalone release. The Soul Is In The Software (2002) refined the sound with sharper production and stronger songwriting, yielding club favorites like "Android," released as a single in 2003, and "Access and Amplify." The 2004 collection UploadedAndRemixed gathered reworkings of the band's material, reflecting how central remix culture was to the scene. Machines Are Us, the third album, pushed toward a harder, more aggressive edge that hinted at the direction LaPlegua would soon take elsewhere, and it was accompanied by the SoundDivE.P.

The band's history is inseparable from LaPlegua's wider output. Even while Icon Of Coil was at its peak, he launched Combichrist, a far more abrasive aggrotech project that would eventually eclipse his original band in popularity, as well as the rock-leaning Panzer AG. Sebastian Komor likewise remained active as a producer and remixer, notably with Zombie Girl. These parallel ventures, combined with heavy touring commitments, effectively placed Icon Of Coil on hiatus after Machines Are Us.

Critically, Icon Of Coil was regarded as one of the strongest bands of the futurepop moment, praised for writing songs that worked as both dancefloor fodder and genuinely catchy pop. Their singles helped define the sound of alternative club nights in the early 2000s, and the band's success put Norway on the map within a scene often dominated by German, Swedish, and Belgian acts.

The project's legacy has been kept alive through occasional reunion performances and revisitations of its catalogue. In 2024 the remix "Devils (Combichrist vs. Icon Of Coil Remix)" explicitly bridged LaPlegua's two best-known projects, and in 2025 a new edition of Serenity Is The Devil marked the debut album's enduring standing among fans of electro-industrial and futurepop.
title: Icon Of Coil
